question.text: Which statement BEST describes the 'fit and proper person' requirement for the sponsor of a Category III AIF under SEBI regulations?

answer.text: Sponsor must have a minimum net worth of INR 50 crore irrespective of corpus size.
Sponsor must be a body corporate registered under the Companies Act, 2013 only.
Sponsor must meet fit-and-proper criteria specified under Schedule II of SEBI (Intermediaries) Regulations, 2008.
Sponsor must have at least 10 years of experience in alternative investments.

explanation.text: **The Logic:** The chapter explicitly requires the sponsor to satisfy the 'fit and proper person' criteria set out in Schedule II of SEBI (Intermediaries) Regulations, 2008. There is no fixed net-worth threshold for the sponsor itself (the INR 10 cr net worth is for the Investment Manager), and the sponsor can be any person or persons including institutions, companies, or individuals. **The Trap:** Option A confuses sponsor eligibility with the Investment Manager's net-worth requirement. Option B wrongly narrows the permitted legal forms. Option D invents a 10-year experience floor not in regulations. **Cross-Exam Context:** XIX-D tests the same Schedule II reference. XXI-B (Portfolio Managers) uses a similar fit-and-proper framework. Compliance exams (III-A) test Schedule II criteria (economic offences, moral turpitude) directly. **Manager's Pro-Tip:** When onboarding a first-time sponsor, pull the Schedule II checklist: integrity, reputation, absence of conviction in economic offences, no SEBI/SAT/court order of restraint. A past adverse SEBI order on a related party is the most common veto. Resolve via sponsor-substitution before PPM filing, not after.
